items.claim: The construction-recurrence claim in device_notes names Jer.33.10, Jer.32.36, and Jer.32.43 as the construction's three book-wide sites but does not disclose that the shared wording collates only at the consonantal-skeleton tier, not at byte or accent-stripped tier.
items.evidence: Jer.33.10's own citation collates at byte tier against the verse. The device_notes claim that the same three-word wording also opens Jer.32.36 and Jer.32.43 does not hold at byte or accent-stripped tier: Jer.32.36 and Jer.32.43 point and accent the phrase differently from Jer.33.10 (a different cantillation on the relative particle and a different vocalization of the participle). The three-verse recurrence is real only once cantillation and niqqud are stripped to the bare consonantal skeleton. The standing rule requires every recurrence claim to name its tier, and a skeleton-only match is the weakest of the three tiers and carries its own named hazard as a contiguous substring search; the row's sweep citation here carries no tier label, sitting immediately beside a byte-tier tag that belongs only to the single-verse quotation, not to the three-verse recurrence it is adjacent to.

items.claim: The row correctly holds the Branch prophecy and the paired Davidic-and-Levitical guarantee together as one span, with its every parashah and cross-tradition disclosure obligation met.
items.evidence: The koh-amar reopening at Jer.33.17 carries no addressee or frame-owner change from the Branch promise it extends, so the granularity rule's requirement of a frame-owner change to license a fresh cut is not met there, and the row is right to hold Jer.33.14-18 as one span. Every Hebrew quotation in the row collates at byte tier against its cited verse. The setumah marks the row discloses at Jer.33.13 (the seam before its own opening), Jer.33.16 (interior), and Jer.33.18 (its own close) match the parashah inventory exactly under the correct mark type, and no other span-relevant mark is left undisclosed. The LXX-absence of the Jer.33.14-26 block is disclosed strictly as cross-tradition metadata carrying no weight for either boundary, keeping the quarantine intact.

items.claim: The row correctly isolates the day-night covenant analogy behind its own fresh, verse-initial word-event onset at Jer.33.19 and defeats the genuine rival of merging it into the preceding Branch material rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: Jer.33.19's vayehi-devar-YHWH formula opens the verse in the ordinary shape (verse-initial, like twenty of the book's twenty-one instances), a primary tier-1 macro-seam device, so the cut is well warranted: the row correctly declines to fold backward into the Branch material despite the topical continuity, because the tier-1 onset controls regardless of theme. The rejected alternative names the genuine maximalist rival (all of Jer.33.14-22 as one continuous consolation) rather than a weaker strawman. The setumah marks disclosed at Jer.33.18 (the seam before) and Jer.33.22 (its own close) match the inventory exactly, and nothing else in the span carries an undisclosed mark. Every Hebrew quotation collates at byte tier, and the LXX-absence of the surrounding block is disclosed strictly as metadata.

items.claim: The row correctly closes the consolation material at the chapter and M7/N8 frame boundary on a fresh word-event onset, with an exclusivity claim that holds at every tier and an accurate ketiv/qere and parashah disclosure.
items.evidence: Jer.33.23's word-event formula is a clean, verse-initial tier-1 onset closing the consolation material at the chapter's own end, which is also the M7/N8 frame seam; the row stops there without straddling it. The claimed two-verse book-wide recurrence of the closing captivity-reversal clause (Jer.33.26 and Jer.32.44, 2 verses book-wide) holds at all three tiers checked -- byte, accent-stripped, and skeleton alike -- a stronger grounding than a match confined to the skeleton tier alone. The ketiv/qere pair on the verb of restoration -- unpointed against pointed forms of the same root -- is correctly identified and matches the single K/Q note the inventory records at Jer.33.26. The setumah marks disclosed at Jer.33.22 (the seam before), Jer.33.24 (interior), and Jer.33.26 (its own close, also the chapter's close) match the inventory exactly.

items.claim: The row correctly opens the N8 frame on Jer.34.1's own word-event header, holds the whole delivered message to Zedekiah as one unit, and correctly names the Jer.34.5 hoy as the vav-prefixed funeral-cry shape rather than a woe onset.
items.evidence: parent_collection flips from the M7 consolation frame to the N8 frame exactly at Jer.34.1, with no straddling on either side of the seam. The contrastive turn at Jer.34.4 carries no addressee or frame-owner change from the envoy commission it extends -- the king stays the addressee throughout -- so the row is right not to cut there despite the shift in tone. The funeral acclamation at Jer.34.5 is explicitly disclosed as the vav-prefixed ve-hoy shape and distinguished in role from the book's woe onsets, day-alas cry, and sword apostrophe, correctly avoiding the misclassification the shape invites. The setumah at Jer.34.5, the petuchah at Jer.34.7, and the paseq at Jer.34.1 all match the inventory exactly, with nothing else in span left undisclosed, and every Hebrew quotation collates at byte tier.

items.claim: The row correctly treats Jer.34.8 as the chapter's own second word-event header and stops before Yahweh's reply at Jer.34.12 on a clean tier-1 onset, with the Jer.34.11 ketiv/qere pair disclosed beside its own quotation.
items.evidence: Jer.34.8 opens its own prose-sermon word-event header, the chapter's second, distinct from the header at Jer.34.1 and correctly treated as its own fresh tier-1 onset rather than folded into the first. The row is right to decline extending forward into Jer.34.12, because that verse opens its own fresh word-event formula -- the same class of primary tier-1 device -- regardless of the topical continuity between the covenant's making and reversal on one side and Yahweh's reply on the other. The ketiv/qere pair on the reversal verb is disclosed immediately beside its own quotation rather than left to a separate note. The petuchah at Jer.34.7 (the seam before) and the setumah at Jer.34.11 (its own close, the same verse carrying the K/Q pair) match the inventory exactly, and every Hebrew quotation collates at byte tier.

items.claim: The observed_substrate_signals field mislabels the word-event formula opening Jer.34.12 as the book's non-initial exception, when both the ruled book-wide inventory and the verse's own bytes show it is an ordinary verse-initial onset.
items.evidence: The row's own quotation of Jer.34.12 gives the verse's full text as וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (byte, re-collated), where the word-event formula's own vayehi is the verse's first word -- the ordinary shape shared by twenty of the book's twenty-one vayehi-devar-YHWH onsets. Of those 21 book-wide instances (20 verse-initial), the ruled inventory names Jer.42.7 as the 1 non-initial exception, and its bytes show why: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (byte, re-collated) opens on a separate temporal clause -- 'and it was, at the end of ten days' -- before the formula's own vayehi appears second in the verse. Jer.34.12 carries no such preceding clause. Tagging Jer.34.12's onset as the non-initial shape in the row's observed_substrate_signals therefore asserts a second exception to a count the inventory fixes at exactly one, a claim neither the inventory nor the verse's own bytes support; the boundary itself is unaffected, since a verse-initial onset is if anything the more ordinary tier-1 warrant.

items.claim: The row correctly holds the Rechabite command, performance, and quoted refusal together as one symbolic-act unit, stopping short of Yahweh's own interpretation only at Jer.35.12's fresh word-event onset, with the Jehoiakim flashback dating properly disclosed against the surrounding Zedekiah-era material.
items.evidence: unit_type as a symbolic-act report matches the vocabulary's own listed example for this chapter. The default rule holding a symbolic act's command, performance, and interpretation as one unit is overridden only at Jer.35.12's own fresh word-event formula, the named tier-1 exception, so the row correctly stops at Jer.35.11 rather than either atomizing the wine-test scene further or absorbing Yahweh's separate interpretation beginning at Jer.35.12. The header's own date clause -- in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah -- is named explicitly against the Zedekiah-era material surrounding it, disclosing the flashback rather than silently smoothing it over. The petuchah marks at Jer.34.22 (the seam before) and Jer.35.11 (its own close) and the paseq at Jer.35.5 match the inventory exactly, and every Hebrew quotation collates at byte tier.
